title: Runtime attention prober: compatibility mesh, bench sweeps, and automated rollback
creator: Aisha Martínez
description: Goal: land a low-risk integration path for FlashAttention v2/v3 variants via a compatibility 'prober' mesh that exercises candidate kernels across representative traffic slices, collects per-kernel telemetry, and drives automated graceful rollback when regressions are detected. This ticket covers the prober harness, bench sweep plan for seq-len/microbatch/tiling, metrics to signal regressions, and a canary/rollback automation policy integrated with Router and Console rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Prober harness merged and enabled behind feature flag (runtime.prober.enable)
End-to-end benchmark matrix executed for FA2/FA3 variants across sequence lengths [32,128,512,1024] and microbatch sizes [1,4,16] with logs stored in cdn-bench-results (S3)
Telemetry emitted: per-request kernel_id, kernel_latency_ms, kernel_error, kv-cache-hit, workspace_bytes; dashboard in Console showing kernel-level p50/p95/p99 and error rate
Canary policy implemented: 5% initial traffic, automated rollback if p99 latency increases >10ms for 512-token median or error rate >0.5% over 10m window
Playbook and runbook updated: how to interpret prober signals, manual rollback steps, and mitigation knobs (disable prober, pin model variant, force kernel-vendor fallback)
Automated GitHub action that gates rollout when performance regressions are detected via benchmark-to-baseline diff and posts result to PRs
comments: 2026-03-01 - A.Martínez: Kickoff. Need to avoid past issues where v3 warmup caused transient p99 regression for prefill-heavy workloads (see ENG-118901). Primary constraint: do not increase noise on live latency SLOs. Proposed: start with off-path prober (duplicate request sampling) and then move to in-path canary if stable.

2026-03-03 - L.O'Connor: Prototype prober implemented in runtime prober branch. It samples 1% of requests and runs them through candidate kernel variants in a shadow decode path; only the primary kernel's response is returned. Early results: FA3 shows 6-9% CPU/workspace variance but no correctness errors on open tests. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1387

2026-03-04 - Perf team (note): Microbench harness added. Script: infra/bench/attn-sweep.py. Runs on a matrix of seqLen x microbatch x tokenTypes. Storing artifacts at s3://rdw-bench/ENG-25678/2026-03-04/. Initial numbers attached to Confluence doc.

2026-03-05 - Design Review (Slack): PM requested thresholds that map to cost & latency impact. Agreed thresholds: p99 delta > 10ms (512 tokens) flagged as high; cost delta > 6% flagged for review. See design notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SERV/ENG-25678+-+Attn+Prober+Design

2026-03-07 - QA: Discovered a race when prober shadow decode reuses KV cache pointers concurrently with primary decode on multi-stream GPUs. Repro steps and test case added to unit test harness. Assigned to ENG-33488 follow-up for safety shim.

2026-03-08 - L.O'Connor: Added workspace-snapshot safety check and backpressure flag to prober to avoid racing deallocations. Updated branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/compare/prober-safety

2026-03-09 - Telemetry: Submitted schema PR for kernel-level fields to observability team. Schema: ['kernel_id','kernel_version','kernel_latency_ms','kernel_error','kv_cache_hit','workspace_bytes']. Indexing set on (kernel_id, region, seq_len). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/526

2026-03-10 - Results: Benchmark run 2026-03-09 shows FA3 has better throughput at seq_len 128 (throughput +12%) but shows a 14ms p99 increase at seq_len 512 when microbatch=1 due to decode startup path. Action: implement staged warmup (prefill warmup jitter) in prober harness and re-run sweeps

2026-03-11 - Roadmap update: Rolling to canary phase planned next week after warmup patch. Automation scope: Router will shift 5% traffic to kernel-variant if prober signals stable for 30m. Rollback automated via console watchdog and GitHub action will block merge if bench-to-baseline regression exceeds thresholds. Follow-up tickets created for rollout automation: ENG-25679 (router integration) and ENG-25680 (console watchdog alerts).
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: Sampling-based prober reduces blast radius versus direct in-path variant but adds execution cost; choose 1% sample initially to limit cost while collecting enough data for p99 signals over 30m windows.

Decision: Use shadow decode (duplicate execution) rather than speculative swap to ensure correctness telemetry without impacting user-visible latency. Speculative swap kept as a longer-term experiment after stable metrics.

Risk: Workspace memory pressure on smaller GPU instances. Mitigation: prober respects workspace_budget and will skip candidate run when workspace_available < threshold. This logic needs to be validated across Dedicated pools.
Operational: Will require increased metrics retention for kernel-level histograms for 72 hours during rollout; consult infra for storage cost estimates before enabling globally.
next_steps: Complete warmup jitter patch and re-run full bench matrix (target: 2026-03-12)
Integrate prober signals with Router canary API (ENG-25679) and Console watchdog (ENG-25680)
Coordinate with infra to enable temporary higher-metric retention and workspace_budget telemetry on Dedicated nodes
Prepare release notes and risk summary for SRE/Support ahead of canary
